title: Security Oncall: Witnessing & Audit Correlation Runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures a pragmatic, oncall-friendly workflow for witnessing security events, capturing forensic evidence, correlating audit logs with RBAC v2 state, and preparing SIEM exports for automated analysis. It is written for security oncall engineers and SREs handling suspected privileged misuse, identity compromise, or suspicious service-to-service behavior.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to incidents where user/service identity or authorization is material (failed/abusive RBAC operations, admin-token misuse, unexpected role elevation).
- Assumes RBAC v2 is deployed and the audit log schema is available in the central audit index.
- Primary SIEM targets: Elastic (internal), Splunk (partner exports).
- Goal: capture auditable evidence fast, avoid contamination, and provide ready-to-ingest artifacts for SIEM and postmortem.

Quick definitions:
- Witnessing: Real-time capture of evidence (logs, API traces) while incident is live.
- Audit record: Structured event produced by control plane (actor, action, target, grant_state, request_id, kv pairs).
- RBAC snapshot: Authorized roles/assignments at a point-in-time.
- Chain-of-custody ledger: Minimal record in ticket describing evidence location and who touched it.

Pre-incident prep (do these before you are paged):
- Verify access: oncall account has read access to /audit/export API and to the RBAC config bucket.
- Scripts in /ops/security: audit-fetch.sh, rbac-snapshot.sh, siem-package.sh (ensure latest version pulled).
- KMS key for evidence packaging is rotated quarterly; ensure your agent has decrypt privileges.
- Add the following saved SIEM queries to the oncall dashboard: suspect-credential-use, mass-privilege-changes, lateral-service-auth.

Immediate triage steps (first 15 minutes):
1) Confirm signal: record alert source, timestamp, initial observable (IP, user, service). Note alert id in ticket.
2) Isolate if needed: for ephemeral service/service tokens, consider revoking the token or isolating the host. Coordinate with SRE.
3) Snapshot RBAC state (important to map what was permitted at time of event):
   - Run: ./rbac-snapshot.sh --out /tmp/rbac-snapshot-$(date +%s).json
   - If script unavailable: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" "https://controlplane.redwood/api/v2/rbac/export?at_time=TIMESTAMP" > /tmp/rbac-snapshot.json
   - Add the snapshot path to ticket and record checksum (sha256).
4) Fetch raw audit events for the window +/- 30m around event_time:
   - ./audit-fetch.sh --from "2024-06-01T10:15:00Z" --to "2024-06-01T11:15:00Z" --out /tmp/audit-window.jsonl
   - Example curl (JSON-lines output):
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" "https://audit.redwood.internal/api/v1/events?from=2024-06-01T10:15:00Z&to=2024-06-01T11:15:00Z" 
       | jq -c '.events[]' > /tmp/audit-window.jsonl
5) Preserve request chains: locate request_id or trace_id fields in events and collect all events with that id.

Evidence capture checklist (minimum required):
- RBAC snapshot file path + sha256
- Audit window JSONL file + sha256
- Representative raw logs from the implicated host/service (if available), compressed and checksummed
- Any API gateway request logs (headers, IPs) exported
- Screenshots or terminal transcripts of exec commands (if oncall performed mitigation)
- Chain-of-custody note appended to ticket: who collected, when, where evidence stored (s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/ID/)

Automated evidence packaging (recommended):
- Use siem-package.sh to prepare artifacts for ingestion: it will normalize timestamps, add metadata (incident_id, collector, host), and encrypt with KMS key.
  ./siem-package.sh --incident ID1234 --inputs "/tmp/audit-window.jsonl,/tmp/rbac-snapshot.json,/tmp/host-logs.tgz" --out /tmp/ID1234-package.enc
- Manual fallback: tar czf /tmp/ID1234-evidence.tgz <files> && gpg --encrypt --recipient security-kms@redwood --output /tmp/ID1234-evidence.gpg /tmp/ID1234-evidence.tgz

SIEM export mapping notes (how fields map to detection rules):
- audit.event_time -> @timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor.id -> user.id (or service.id)
- actor.type -> user.type (human | service)
- action -> event.action (create, update, delete, assume_role, auth_fail)
- target.resource -> resource.name
- grant_state -> auth.grant_state (granted | denied | expired)
- request_id,trace_id -> event.id (correlation)
- meta.ip,meta.user_agent -> source.ip, user_agent

Example Splunk query to find privilege escalation patterns (oncall quick):
index=audit OR index=proxy "action=assume_role" OR "role:admin" | stats count by actor.id, target.resource, action | where count > 3

Example Elastic DSL (pseudo) to get all events correlated by request_id:
POST /audit/_search
{
  "query": {
    "term": {"request_id": "abc-123-request"}
  },
  "sort": [{"@timestamp": "asc"}]
}

Correlating RBAC state with events:
- For each event where action is grant/revoke/assume_role, cross-reference the RBAC snapshot to verify whether the actor had that ability at event_time.
- If event shows a grant that did not exist in snapshot, mark as suspicious and escalate.
- If actor is a service account, check linked deployments and recent code deploys (could be automated via CI: check pipeline run IDs).

Containment play (if confirmed malicious):
- Short term: revoke API token / session, remove temporary role binding, block source IPs at edge.
- Medium term: rotate affected keys, rotate service account tokens, require re-auth for affected users.
- Document every action in ticket and append audit evidence generated during mitigation.

Escalation matrix (example):
- Level 1 (oncall sec): triage, collect evidence, snapshot RBAC, contain.
- Level 2 (sec incident lead): declare incident, coordinate with SRE for host isolation, notify legal if PII suspected.
- Level 3 (CISO + exec): breaches impacting customers, regulatory exposure, or data exfiltration.

Post-incident: lightweight postmortem checklist:
- Did we capture unambiguous audit records for the time window? (Y/N) If no, why not?
- Saved RBAC snapshot attached? (Y/N)
- Evidence package uploaded to evidence bucket and ticket updated with location+checksum? (Y/N)
- Were detection rules updated to prevent recurrence? (List rule ids)
- Action items assigned with owners and due dates.

Notes & gotchas (lessons from prior incidents):
- Audit events may be sampled for high-volume paths; if you see gaps, escalate to infra to re-run full export from persistence layer.
- RBAC mutations can be transient (create-then-delete within seconds). The snapshot must be taken as early as possible; if you wait, the state may have changed.
- Watch for service-to-service token reuse: actor.type==service + origin_ip not in known pool is high risk.

References and utilities:
- /ops/security/audit-fetch.sh (fetches from audit API, supports time windows)
- /ops/security/rbac-snapshot.sh (exports RBAC v2 state at given timestamp)
- SIEM ingestion mapping: confluence page (linked in linked_artifacts)
- Contact list: security-oncall rotation (Slack: #sec-oncall), SRE pager (SRE-pager)

Appendix: quick regexes and commands (copy-paste friendly)
- Grab events for user alice@example.com: jq -c 'select(.actor.email=="alice@example.com")' /tmp/audit-window.jsonl > /tmp/alice-events.jsonl
- Extract request ids: jq -r '.request_id' /tmp/alice-events.jsonl | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
- Compute checksum: sha256sum /tmp/ID1234-package.enc > /tmp/ID1234-package.enc.sha256

If anything in this runbook is unclear during an incident, treat the safety-first path: collect more raw data (don't delete), document actions, and escalate to a sec lead.
